summary: Pebble (formerly T2), a Twitter-like microblogging startup, is shutting down after peaking at 3,000 daily active users out of 20,000 registered. Its founders blame a crowded field of Twitter rivals, the durable network effect of X, no native mobile app, a rebrand that softened the value proposition, and a space that was perhaps too safe. The website closes November 1st, users can export their archives, and the founders may work together on something new.
one_line: Twitter alternative Pebble, formerly T2, is shutting down after peaking at 3,000 daily users, citing competition, X's network effect, and an overly safe community.
key_facts: Pebble (formerly T2) is shutting down, described as the first casualty among Twitter alternatives.
The app maxed out at 3,000 daily active users out of 20,000 registered users, and daily users fell to 1,000 after the rebrand from T2.
Pebble's retention was 30% by week four, and 60% of people who received an invite converted to become users.
About 10,000 users came to its invite list from early press, including coverage of its first outside funding, a $1.1 million angel round.
Angel investors included former Google VP Bradley Horowitz, Android co-founder Rich Miner, and former Wikipedia CEO Katherine Maher.
Similarweb data indicates the Pebble website topped 99,300 visits last month.
Co-founder and CEO Gabor Cselle said the competitive landscape evolved faster than expected, with many established organizations and newcomers doing similar things.
CTO Michael Greer said the durability of Twitter's network effect is stronger than anticipated; Threads and others have faced this as well.

Pebble bet on trust, safety and moderation and was 'kinder, safer'; co-founder Sarah Oh, Twitter's former human rights advisor, was on the team. The founders now think it went too far into 'kindness' territory and lacked breaking news and conversation.
Pebble lacked a native mobile app, as T2 prioritized the web, which lost app-store discovery; Greer said 'that might have been a mistake.'
Cselle questioned whether the rebrand from T2 to Pebble softened the value proposition.
Users can export their Pebble archive as a zip file that loads a mini web page of their old posts; the website shuts down on November 1st.
Pebble is returning a small amount of leftover funds to investors, and there are no further plans for the IP at this time.
The winddown was announced to users at 9 AM PT on the day of the article.
